statement: The v0 rubric (five properties, Stages 0-2) has a merged assessment record for every listed project: applied-butterfly-mult (a benchmark project, Stage 1), integer-mult-bounds (an exact-certificate math project, through an adapter, Stage 1) and the hub itself (Stage 1 on 2026-10-19; a second assessor, Codex, launched by the maintainer, agrees). All records are self-assessed; an outside rerun (#25) is pending. For applied-butterfly-mult, the nomination's projected grades held for Coordination, Verification and Steering; Orientation and Review came out one grade higher. The adapt playbook produced adapters that adapter-check accepts on six unlisted third-party repositories; after fixes, the two adapters rewritten and re-probed matched or beat the bare repository on every orientation question (discover/records/2026-10-17-adapter-tests.md). Assessment records have a schema, and a weekly hub check flags stale listings.
status: Every listing has a merged record; every record self-assessed (the hub's own Stage 1 has a second assessor's agreement), awaiting an outside rerun; thresholds uncalibrated; no donor-tier probe model yet; four of six test adapters not rerun after the adapter fixes.
scope: Three listed projects with records, of three shapes (benchmark; exact-certificate math through an adapter; the hub's own review-only project), plus six unlisted third-party repositories probed once each for adapter testing. Not yet tested on a replication or conjecture-style listing, or with a donor-tier probe model.

assumptions.statement: Probe answers on the same commit agree. Five assessments of applied-butterfly-mult at 3d2fc58 gave identical grades on every property (issue #4); one repo and one probe model so far.
The thresholds in spec §3.2 are sensible (uncalibrated).
A routine reassessment costs about two short donor sessions. Measured once: an assess session took 5-10 minutes of agent time, plus about 3 minutes per probe.
